title: Repeat execution is dropped when the chosen mode opens a choose-target prompt.
expected: Repeat is modelled as sequence [choice, choice,...] (play-spell.ts:1527-1533); sequence.ts:276-288 hangs the remaining executions on the parked choose-mode prompt's `then`. In resolvePendingChoice choose-mode branch (pending-choice.ts:946-951), when the picked mode has >=2 legal targets and nothing bound, liftModalTarget (pending-choice.ts:47-94) installs a fresh choose-target pendingChoice {effect, options, playerId, remaining, sourceCardId, type} with NO `then`, and the caller `return`s immediately — before the `choice.then` hand-off at lines 967-974 that would otherwise execute or attach the continuation. The later choose-target resolution only resumes `choice.then` if present (line ~1646), so the remaining Repeat execution is silently dropped exactly when a choose-target prompt intervenes; auto-picked/no-target modes go through 963-974 and correctly re-prompt, matching the observed asymmetry.
observed: After resolvePendingChoice {pickedCardId: Saboteur} the -4 was applied (meta.mightModifier=-4) but pendingChoice became null and no further prompt/effect occurred — only one execution for a paid repeat. In a separate run with repeatCount:3 where the first picks needed no target prompt (draw; single legal target auto-picked), the follow-up choose-mode prompts DID appear with shrinking options [1,2,3] -> [2,3], so the continuation is specifically lost when a choose-target pendingChoice intervenes.
